# Transmission Lines

## Introduction

A transmission line is a two-conductor structure that guides electromagnetic energy
from one point to another.

## Telegrapher's Equations

The distributed-parameter model gives:

$$\frac{\partial V}{\partial z} = -\left(R + j\omega L\right) I$$

$$\frac{\partial I}{\partial z} = -\left(G + j\omega C\right) V$$

where $R$, $L$, $G$, $C$ are the per-unit-length parameters.

## Propagation Constant

$$\gamma = \alpha + j\beta = \sqrt{(R + j\omega L)(G + j\omega C)}$$

## Characteristic Impedance

$$Z_0 = \sqrt{\frac{R + j\omega L}{G + j\omega C}}$$

For a lossless line ($R = G = 0$):

$$Z_0 = \sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}$$
